# NASA 3D asset sources

- `hubble-space-telescope-a.glb` — [Hubble Space Telescope (A)](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/hubble-space-telescope-a/), source credited by NASA to DigitalSpace Corporation. Used as the visual observatory in the playable telescope servicing campaign. T-MINUS keeps its fictional servicing task and interaction geometry.
- `1999-rq36-asteroid.glb` — [1999 RQ36 asteroid](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/1999-rq36-asteroid/), source credited by NASA to Christopher R. Meaney. Used only as a visual shape reference for one boulder on fictional Planet B. Its placement, size, and planetary setting are fictional.
- `../vendor/DRACOLoader.js` and `../vendor/draco/` — Three.js r170 Draco loader and decoder, from [Three.js](https://github.com/mrdoob/three.js/tree/r170/examples/jsm/libs/draco). Required by the Hubble GLB.

NASA's [3D Resources page](https://science.nasa.gov/3d-resources/) says the models are available to download and use and refers users to its [Images and Media Usage Guidelines](https://www.nasa.gov/nasa-brand-center/images-and-media/). These models are visual assets, not observational datasets or validated flight geometry.
